import { CodeBlock } from '../../components/ui';

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="a-map-not-a-deployment"><a href="#a-map-not-a-deployment">A map, not a deployment</a></h2>

The homepage diagram explains relationships: Abbey is a companion direction; ABI provides orchestration and runtime foundations; WDBX supplies semantic storage associated with that runtime. Selecting a layer changes an explanation, not a running system.

Cloud backends are optional according to the ABI README. The diagram does not imply that all integrations are configured, that every data path is implemented, or that a production cluster has been verified.

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="products-and-personas"><a href="#products-and-personas">Products and personas</a></h2>

ABI as a software product and Abi as a governance persona are different axes. Likewise, Aviva is described as a direct expert mode, not an independently verified standalone repository. Keep those distinctions visible in copy, APIs, and UI labels.

The existing MLAI contracts distinguish product accents from persona colors. This design uses violet for the ABI product and does not use that color to assert a persona identity.

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="gama-is-a-separate-track"><a href="#gama-is-a-separate-track">Gama is a separate track</a></h2>

Gama focuses on declarative application UI in Swift. Its retained-tree and scene model addresses application rendering, not the Rust runtime’s backend selection or WDBX persistence.

An integration may be an interesting future idea, but an attractive diagram is not evidence that it already exists. Proposed relationships should remain labeled until a concrete implementation and appropriate verification support them.

</section>
